body:
> The maximum number of simultaneous sounds this node can play.

"_At the same time_" was a fine and intuitive way to express the concept. "_Simultaneous_" means the same thing but introduces a more complex term for no benefit.
The class reference, especially for these very common classes, should be accessible to users with all sorts of backgrounds in the English language.

> Increasing this value allows multiple sounds to overlap (e.g., rapid gunfire or echoes), but at a higher CPU cost.

This line is redundant, as it repeats the same concept mentioned in the first line (that multiple sounds can be played at the same time).
The "_increased CPU cost_" is not particularly unusual. More things happening means more CPU power is consumed. So this information is also redundant.

> When the limit is reached, playing a new sound will instantly terminate the oldest active sound to stay within the limit.

This last added line gives the illusion of being more meaningful, but in practice it is saying the same thing as "_Playing additional sounds after this value is reached will cut off the oldest sounds._", which was present in the original description.

body:
Perhaps a few example use cases could be added, so long as they don't break the flow of the existing two sentences.

However, this is the kind of "thing" whose purpose is easier to understand if other descriptions are improved, instead.

What I mean to say is, I remember that I completely overhauled [AudioStreamPlayer](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/81858)'s descriptions in the past, but these changes were never carried over to the 2D and 3D equivalents. Among the changes was to make it *as clear as possible* that the node was capable of playing more than one sound at once, by implying it numerous times.

For example (these are just snippets):
> Stops **the audio** -> Stops **all sounds**
> Plays **the audio** -> Plays **a sound**
> Returns whether the AudioStreamPlayer can return the AudioStreamPlayback -> Returns true if **any sound** is active
